cards.text: In the year that King Ahaz dies, a burden is received. Ahaz was king of Judah (2 Kings 16:1), and this message from the LORD is for the Philistines, who lived along the seacoast (Zephaniah 2:5). Friend, when your mail is literally called a BURDEN, you open it slow.
First thing the message brings up: the rod that struck the Philistines is broken. You'd think it's party time. Streamers. Cookies. The whole thing.

cards.question: The message tells the Philistines to rejoice that the rod that struck them is broken.
The Philistines are told not to rejoice, because something will spring from the root of the snake. What is it?
A viper from the snake's root, and a flying serpent from its egg. What's that picture telling the Philistines?

answers.text: The danger is gone for good

cards.text: Then the message turns to a whole different crowd: the poor and the needy. The firstborn of the poor will find pasture. Same message, totally different envelope.

cards.question: The firstborn of the poor will find pasture. What does the message say about the needy?

answers.text: They will lie down in safety

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to the Philistines, and it is NOT pasture. He says, 'I will kill your root.' Oh, friend. That's the kind of sentence you read twice and then sit down.

cards.question: The LORD says He will kill the Philistines' root. How?
The LORD says whatever is left of the Philistines, their remnant, will be spared.

cards.text: Now the message gets LOUD: "Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Melt away, all you Philistines!" That's not a weather report, baker. That's a SIREN.

cards.question: The gate wails and the city cries out because a cloud of smoke is coming. From which direction?
The cloud of smoke from the north has no stragglers in its ranks. That means nobody in its ranks falls ___.

cards.text: Last line. Envoys from that nation come, and the question is what answer they'll be given. The answer starts like this: "The LORD has founded Zion…"

cards.question: The envoys are told the LORD has founded Zion. What will His afflicted people find there?

cards.text: Smoke from the north, wailing at the gate, and right in the middle of it, a refuge the LORD Himself founded. Baker, a stamper who spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer knows exactly how good that word sounds.

findings.problem: The story card has five sentences: one full sentence followed by four fragments ('You'd think it's party time.' 'Streamers.' 'Cookies.' 'The whole thing.'). Non-opening story cards are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Something more dangerous is coming' adds a comparison the text never makes. Isaiah 14:29 says a viper will spring from the snake's root and a flying serpent from its egg. It never says the new threat is worse. An answer like 'The danger isn't over' stays with what the text says.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences, one more than the limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke 'Same message, totally different envelope' doesn't match the action. In the text, one message turns to a different group of people. A different envelope suggests different packaging, not a different recipient, so the image doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences ('Then the LORD speaks…' / 'He says…' / 'Oh, friend.' / 'That's the kind of sentence…'), two more than the limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The quoted words 'I will kill your root.' end with a period that isn't in the BSB. The verse reads 'but I will kill your root by famine,' with no period after 'root.' The quote also uses single quotation marks, which the script's exact-wording check may miss.

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The story card has five sentences: the three quoted lines plus two of Papa Dorin's own ('That's not a weather report, baker.' 'That's a SIREN.').

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says 'The gate wails and the city cries out,' which turns the text's commands into events. Isaiah 14:31 says 'Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city!' The question should keep these as commands, for example 'The gate is told to wail because…'.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences ('Last line.' / 'Envoys from that nation come…' / 'The answer starts like this…'), one more than the limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card mostly recaps verses that earlier cards already covered (the smoke from the north, the gate, the refuge in Zion) and doesn't move the passage forward. Its citation, Isaiah 14:31-32, also points back to verses that were already told.

Two problems with what the text calls things. 'Wailing at the gate' turns the command 'Wail, O gate!' into an event. 'Right in the middle of it, a refuge the LORD Himself founded' places Zion in the middle of the smoke, which the text never says, and says the LORD founded a refuge when Isaiah 14:32 says He founded Zion, where His afflicted people will find refuge.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 6 of the 9 choice cards are multiple choice, 2 are true or false, and only 1 is fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
